For a period of time I took care of management of passive funds. The most difficult to manage in the presence of illiquid stocks/markets. 

Stock price goes up. Its weight in the fund increases. You need to reduce and rebalance according to the weight in the benchmark. But the stock moved up on thin volume and you have large quantity to reduce. 

You can only deviate certain basis points from the benchmark.

So many indexed/passive funds out there...

Index providers add/remove stocks from the benchmarks.

Fund managers need to follow and rebalance.

A pick up in volume and transactions...

Is the volume spike meaningful data point?

Think of the same in small or mid cap stocks when funds get involved...

Is it the market or few large portfolio's decision?

Open-source AI is undercutting Big AI's margins.

Even amid the rapid scale of AI, open-source models cost far less per token, the basic unit of AI computing.

For example, Anthropic’s Fable 5 model was more than 50 times more expensive per token than DeepSeek’s V4 Pro.

Other open-source models from Alibaba, Moonshot AI, and Nvidia are also competing at a fraction of the cost of leading proprietary models.

As cheaper alternatives improve, proprietary AI companies will face increasing pressure to lower prices.

This could potentially squeeze profit margins all as CapEx is surging.

Keep watching open-source AI.

On agents:

Dealing with real estate agents is like dealing with brokers in listed equities. Don't even ask their opinion. You need to do your own homework. 

Talk to other owners in the area. This is something I always do. 

With stocks, charts are my go to source. 

Have a plan. Read. Investigate. Fish for crucial information when dealing with agents. I.e. how long has the property been listed? What was the last offer? How many owners on the title deed (more owners more difficulty in agreement)? Is it a seller or buyer market? What is going on with yields? Are banks easy on lending?
